stem:
The diagram shows Earth on about 21 June. Kiara compares daytime length at place P near the North Pole, place E on the Equator, and place S in the Southern Hemisphere.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Around 21 June the Northern Hemisphere has its longest day.
At the Equator there are about 12 hours of daylight and 12 hours of darkness.
The Northern Hemisphere's longest day occurs at the March equinox.
After 21 June, Northern Hemisphere days become longer and nights become shorter.

teacher.key_rationale: Around 21 June the Northern Hemisphere has its longest day, while the equator stays near 12 hours day and night. The March equinox is not that longest day, and after 21 June northern days shorten.
teacher.figure_note: Earth on 21 June with equator E, northern place P, southern place S, and sunlight arrows.
